clinical_category: Chronic liver disease - hepatitis A and B vaccination
blueprint_topic: Preventive vaccination teaching for adults with chronic liver disease
stem: A 64-year-old client with cirrhosis has no documentation of hepatitis A or hepatitis B vaccination. Which teaching by the nurse is most appropriate?

options.A: Review the current CDC vaccination recommendations with the client and arrange completion of indicated hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccine series because chronic liver disease is a specific indication/risk factor.
options.B: Vaccination is unnecessary because hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccines are recommended only for healthcare personnel with occupational exposure.
options.C: One dose of either vaccine guarantees complete lifelong protection, so there is no reason to complete the recommended series.
options.D: Chronic liver disease is a contraindication to hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccination because vaccination can worsen cirrhosis.

rationale: A is correct. The current CDC adult immunization schedule identifies chronic liver disease as an indication for hepatitis A vaccination because these clients are at increased risk for severe outcomes from hepatitis A infection. For hepatitis B, adults age 60 years or older with risk factors for HBV infection—including chronic liver disease—should receive a HepB vaccine series. The current CDC adult schedule remains the July 2, 2025 schedule under the March 16, 2026 court order, with the schedule page explicitly identifying it as current in 2026. B is incorrect because hepatitis vaccination recommendations extend well beyond occupational risk. C is incorrect because the recommended vaccine course depends on product and requires completion of the indicated series; a single dose should not be presented as guaranteeing complete lifelong protection. D is incorrect because chronic liver disease is an indication/risk factor supporting vaccination, not a blanket contraindication. The final item uses an age and disease state that make both HepA and HepB recommendations directly supported by current CDC guidance.
educational_objective: Teach adults with chronic liver disease to receive indicated hepatitis A and hepatitis B vaccination according to the current CDC adult immunization schedule rather than assuming vaccination is limited to occupational-risk groups or completed after one dose.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)
source_document_title: Adult Immunization Schedule by Medical Condition and Other Indication; Adult Immunization Schedule Notes; Vaccines in the Adult Immunization Schedule
source_version_date: July 2, 2025 adult schedule remains the current CDC adult schedule in 2026 pursuant to the March 16, 2026 preliminary court order; current pages accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: CDC 'Vaccines in the Adult Immunization Schedule' → notice stating that, pursuant to the March 16, 2026 preliminary order, the July 2, 2025 adult schedule is the current CDC Adult Immunization Schedule. CDC 'Adult Immunization Schedule by Medical Condition and Other Indication' → Chronic liver disease/alcoholism column: HepA recommended based on increased risk/severe outcome; HepB recommended with risk indication. CDC 'Adult Immunization Schedule Notes' → Hepatitis A special situations: chronic liver disease is a risk factor for severe HAV disease; Hepatitis B: adults age 60 years or older with known risk factors, including chronic liver disease, should receive a HepB series.
source_claim_supported: Current CDC guidance directly supports HepA vaccination for adults with chronic liver disease and HepB vaccination for adults age 60 or older with chronic liver disease as an HBV risk factor; CDC explicitly identifies the July 2, 2025 adult schedule as the current schedule in 2026 under the March 16, 2026 court order.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance, printed p. 9 (PDF p. 13): related activity statements include 'Educate client about preventive care and health maintenance recommendations,' adult health education, and assessment/education regarding health risks.
correction_summary: Rebuilt the source's generic vaccine-benefit recall question into an applied preventive-care decision using a 64-year-old client with cirrhosis, which makes both HepA and HepB recommendations directly supported by current CDC guidance. Added currentness verification explaining why the July 2, 2025 schedule remains the current CDC adult schedule in 2026 and removed the vague claim of universal vaccine protection after one dose.
audit_findings: The source concept was valid but too generic and cited only a CDC vaccines homepage rather than the current adult schedule and notes.
Fresh CDC review verifies that the July 2, 2025 adult immunization schedule remains the current schedule in 2026 under the March 16, 2026 court order.
CDC directly identifies chronic liver disease as an indication for HepA and as a HepB risk factor; using age 64 makes the HepB recommendation unambiguous under the current schedule.
Distractors test occupational-only restriction, single-dose overclaim, and false contraindication from cirrhosis; none is defensible.
